newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks storm to record closing high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks storm to record closing high.

text.p: Bolstered by Wall Street's strength and a firm dollar, French stocks stormed to a new closing record high in strong volume.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 32.73 points or 1.23 percent at 2,698.92. But that was below a historic high hit earlier in the day of 2,711.12. The CAC-40 futures contract ended 31 points higher at 2,704.
Volume totalled a robust 13.2 billion francs.
Dealers said the buying was fueled by North American and British demand. Domestic investors had turned cautious, believing that the market was toppy, they said.

Aluminium producer Pechiney, which reported after the close a 1996 net loss of 2.98 billion francs against a profit of 1.47 billion francs, gained 4.25 percent to 267.10 francs. The 1996 loss included restructuring provisions of 3.69 billion francs.
French bank BNP, which announced after the close a 116 percent jump in net profit to 3.86 billion francs, gained 2.91 percent to 272.20 francs in anticipation of a strong performance.
Shares in holding company Paribas and its units Cie Bancaire and Cetelem gained on continued speculation about a restructuring in the financial sector.
Paribas was up 1.68 percent to 394.50 francs. Cie Bancaire rose 5.45 percent to 793 francs and Cetelem climbed 3.47 percent to 745 francs.
Renault reversed its day's losses to finish up 0.43 percent at 139.80 francs amid a growing belief the carmaker would not reverse its decision to shut its Belgian plant, traders said.
Retailer Pinault-Printemps fell 0.78 percent to 2.405 francs after a British brokerage sold shares, one market source said.
